The filmmakers could have done more with the story if they really wanted to. And they didn't because they didn't have to.
Project Hail Mary is like E.T. written by someone from MIT, a smart film with a lot of heart.
The Bride is trying too hard to be edgy, but it's just loud.
Hoppers is Pixar's weirdest and best movie in years.
Scream 7 is a straightforward cash grab.

media_title: Tyler Perry's Joe's College Road Trip
rt_quote: Tyler Perry's Joe's College Road Trip feels like it's trying too hard to earn that hard R rating.
Wuthering Heights is Bridgerton with a touch of Fifty Shades of Grey, directed by Tim Burton. The insanity of the characters is what kept me in the story.
The animation and art direction in GOAT are gorgeous. The story is just there as a one-word joke.
Send Help is Sam Raimi back to having fun. The film uses stereotypes for comedy, but it doesn't use that as an excuse to not give the characters some depth.
Return to Silent Hill does a great disservice to Silent Hill 2, which many consider to be one of the greatest video game narratives of all time.
Mercy is a Black Mirror episode without the cleverness. The film presents the technology as darkly questionable, and then says nothing about it.
The direction and acting make the material better than it actually is.
The characters are better written this time around, and Nia DaCosta's direction is amazing.
Primate knows what it is. Real work and craftsmanship was put into certain parts of this movie, probably way more than they needed to.
A good filmmaker can take a character that you might hate, but will make you root for them because of the situation you're watching. That's exactly what Josh Safdie does with Marty Supreme.
For a movie that combines action, comedy, and horror, it's soft.
Avatar: Fire and Ash's story is too familiar, but it's still a highly entertaining film, and James Cameron is an amazing director.
The Housemaid is trash, but I'd be d*mned if it's not some good trash.

I dislike Five Nights at Freddy's 2 more than the first one. The more that they try to make these animatronic costumes look scary, the more ridiculous they get. I've seen school mascots that look more intimidating.
There is so much imagination that goes into these environments, and they always find a joke to do with the ecosystem or the office humor.
Wicked: For Good falls short of the last movie. Is it still entertaining? Yes, it is.
Playdate is the worst movie of 2025 because it's so annoying. There is not one likeable character in the whole film.
The Running Man never goes full Edgar Wright. It's a fun action movie, but it doesn't play to the director's strengths.
Tyler Perry's most boring movie.
Dan Trachtenberg is taking really bold steps with the Predator franchise—expanding the world and making these creatures real characters.
The strength of the film is the conflict between Emma Stone and Jesse Plemons. Not everyone will love the ending, but it takes an approach that I wish more films would.
Shelby Oaks has strong atmosphere and striking sets. The main character makes a lot of dumb decisions. She's the typical "don't do that" horror person.
Frankenstein is a gorgeous film with a beautiful performance by Jacob Elordi.
Black Phone 2 feels very derivative of A Nightmare on Elm Street. The standout is Scott Derrickson's direction, which adds to the creepiness of the film.
Tron: Ares follows the same formula as the previous Tron movies: beautiful visuals, great music, and a weak story.
The Smashing Machine features some of Dwayne Johnson's best acting in years. The rest of the movie is not as memorable.
Marlon Wayans' performance is incredible. However, the film is so wrapped up in the visuals that it doesn't concentrate on the script or the characters.
As brutal as this movie is, there is a lot of heart.
Jeffrey Wright steals every scene he's in.
The Conjuring: Last Rites falls short of being a great send-off for the Warrens.
The Toxic Avenger reboot was made out of respect for Troma. The film keeps the tone of the original but also does it's own thing.
Ne Zha II has the most epic scope of any animated film I've ever seen. I've never seen anything like it.
Nobody 2 has very good character introductions, set ups, and twists with the alliances.
Weapons is an unorthodox horror movie. The ending is nuts!
The Bad Guys 2 is chaotic without feeling out of control. Sam Rockwell continues to provide great voice work for Mr. Wolf.
Once Freakier Friday starts to pull back on the comedy, Jamie Lee Curtis and Lindsay Lohan's performances really start to shine.
No effort was put into this COVID-era adaptation of The War of the Worlds.
The Naked Gun is the dumbest movie of the year, and I laughed the whole time.

media_title: I Know What You Did Last Summer
rt_quote: These characters are uninteresting and some of the dumbest people I've seen in a horror movie in a long time.

The Fantastic Four: First Steps is one of Marvel's best-looking movies, although the story isn't as interesting as the visuals. Julia Garner's performance as Shalla-Bal has the most complex emotional scenes.
They keep trying to make the Smurfs hip instead of telling a good story. The Smurfs are dancing to hip-hop beats and making modern jokes. It feels like old people trying to be cool.
Tyler Perry has made a movie so bad, even Madea can't save it. Most of this "movie" is just a commercial for the Atlantis resort in the Bahamas.
This is definitely James Gunn's Superman, which means it leans on not just humor, but his humor. It's not just the most comic book Superman that we've had - it's a cartoon.
The Old Guard 2 looks cheap compared to the first movie. The characters travel around the world and make that seem boring.
Bursting with charm and genuine heart, Halle & Regé-Jean prove to be the romcom pairing worth fighting for.

BTS: The Return is a timely reflection of the transparent strategy for the algorithm instead of artistic expression. BTS broke through but an exploration of how the members felt about new bands as well as their solo success would have been interesting.
Sirāt achieves its biggest impacts through its sound design but ultimately leaves the story feeling incomplete.

media_title: We Need to Talk About Kevin
rt_quote: Dark and unsettling, We Need to Talk About Kevin keeps you on edge, even if its constant time jumps dilute some of the emotional punch. Still, it’s a gripping, nail-biting watch anchored by brilliant performances.
Ratcatcher pairs realism with quiet, lingering emotion. Some moments are unsettling without clear explanation, but its portrait of guilt, innocence, and poverty is deeply affecting.
A fun entry that doesn’t take itself too seriously. What we get is heart, charm, and a Predator you actually want to root for. A bold take on the franchise and it doesn’t miss.

Entertaining and sure to get people talking, One Battle After Another shines. Peel back the veneer, though, and you find underdeveloped Black characters meant to be at the heart of the revolution, yet we see so little of their story or motivation.

Polished and well-made, Weapons hooks you early with its concept and characters. But too many shifting perspectives dilute the story, leading to a final act that feels disillusioning. Still, expect it to be all the rage.

media_title: Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba Infinity Castle
rt_quote: An action-fueled first act, with stunning visuals made for the big screen. Buckle up, Infinity Castle plunges you into a breathtaking descent where every emotion hits hard.
A sharp whodunit hook draws you in, even for newcomers. The pacing lingers too long at times, but the intrigue lasts just enough to keep you chasing answers.
James Gunn delivers a Superman unafraid to grapple with global issues, painting an unmistakable allegory. It’s bold, resonant, and powered by a truly terrific co-star.
In trying to broaden its appeal, Megan loses some of the bite that made the original pop. Still, its campy energy delivers just enough to keep it entertaining.
The teachings of Orwell take a more tragic poetic turn for audiences as his historical views prove to still be challenging for well-meaning people today.
It Was Just an Accident is bold in theme and rich in empathy, drawing you into its characters’ moral dilemmas and delivering a quietly powerful payoff.

Silver Bullet is a heartwarming story with a strong sense of place and flawed but lovable characters. The werewolf effects and gore are certainly adequate, but it’s the story and characters that make this one of the best werewolf films of all time.

Scary Movie’s jokes can be hit, miss, or downright offensive; but enough of them land to make for an enjoyable watch. The movie shines brightest with the jokes that most resemble the absurdism of spoofs like Airplane and The Naked Gun.

The effectiveness of Undertone’s sonic assault is undeniable, but much of the film’s suspense comes from its visuals. Viewers are immersed in negative spaces, gazing at out of focus background images that could start moving at any moment.

media_title: Ready or Not 2: Here I Come
rt_quote: Ready or Not 2 continues the light-hearted, bloody humor of the first film, anchored by a committed performance from Weaving. Themes of a world controlled by the ultra-wealthy have only become more relevant in the 6 years since the original’s release.

His House is a story of guilt, loss, and the challenges of assimilating to another culture. It demonstrates fiction’s ability to foster empathy, and proves there is value in using a well-orchestrated scare-fest as a vessel for such powerful themes.

It’s fascinating to see the roots of the slasher genre on display throughout A Bay of Blood, but the scattered plot and vast array of one note characters make this film difficult to enjoy despite the gory kills and Bava’s skill as a cinematographer.

The film’s best attribute is its puppet effects, but their impact is lost in an unnecessarily complicated and poorly explained plot. So much time is spent on an unnecessary psychic aspect of the story that our main character is barely a character at all.

Though The Blob’s jaw-dropping practical effects are its main draw, the film’s script does a great job of developing a fun cast of small town characters while working in some humor and charm along the way.

What Friday the 13th lacks in plot, it makes up for in grit and atmosphere. The realism of Savini’s practical effects and the film’s slow pacing work in tandem to build a suspense that the rest of the franchise cannot match.
Silent Night Deadly Night has the same bones as the original, but it unlocks additional character depth and emotion by adding a new element to Billy’s murders of the people he deems to be naughty.

This remake has none of the charm or atmosphere of the original. Its frenetic cinematography, shallow characters, and barebones plot make it extremely difficult to engage with or even pay attention to for its full runtime.

Train to Busan has everything you could want from a zombie film - great effects, tense action, and most importantly, a core of authentic characters that drive home the film’s powerful emotions and themes.

Send Help is a fun ride, anchored by wonderful performances from McAdams and O’Brien. The plot takes some questionable and sometimes frustrating twists and turns, but the entertaining set pieces and character depth keep the film afloat.

Annabelle: Creation is one of the scarier films in the The Conjuring Universe, but like other films in the franchise, it lacks both a compelling plot and compelling characters in the absence of the Warrens.

The Bone Temple organically continues the narrative of its predecessor while adding new elements and themes that make the film a standout in the franchise. The film ups the menace despite the bold choice to de-emphasize the infected as the main threat.

The Coffee Table perfectly balances its tone to make its horrific subject matter not only bearable but darkly comedic. Incredible performances further contribute to the unique tone that is masterfully struck by Casas.

Signs succeeds not only as a suspenseful alien invasion film, but as a deeply moving family drama. Great dialogue and characters pull the viewer into the emotional core of the story, and make the tension all the more poignant.
Perkins squanders some interesting creature design and legitimately creepy moments by directing two bizarre performances that tank the viewer’s interest in the film almost immediately.

The folksy characters typical of the Coens’ work are perfectly juxtaposed against the ruthlessness of Bardem’s incomparable performance. Both the landscape and soundscape are simultaneously barren and rich, mirroring the understated yet powerful dialogue.

Del Toro succeeds in creating a visually rich world in which the story unfolds. As for capturing the human element of the story, his success is muted by the emotional whiplash in the film's conclusion, and some unearned yet beautifully scripted dialogue.
Shelby Oaks is a fairly paint-by-numbers affair, but it manages to squeeze some suspense and scares out of its familiar formula.
John Carpenter’s score and Dean Cundey’s cinematography elevate Halloween to a genre-defining classic. Its style and atmosphere are still unrivaled by any of the imitators released in its wake
House's biggest strength and weakness is that it is utterly disorienting which can be very engaging for the viewer but can also keep you from being grounded in the film.

Black Phone 2 focuses on the prior film’s heroes while avoiding a rehash of the same plot. Its character-centric approach and creepy atmosphere saves it from being a mere ripoff of either its predecessor, or of a certain iconic film with a similar plot.

Color Out of Space meets the visual challenges inherent in adapting H.P. Lovecraft, but the entertainment value is dampened by the lack of any engaging story, relationship, or chemistry between the characters.

media_title: A Nightmare on Elm Street 5: The Dream Child
rt_quote: The Dream Child has good ideas, and is entertaining despite its flaws. Partly a victim of a rushed production, and partly of extensive MPAA cuts, the final product is a slapdash jumble of what could have been a far more compelling entry in the franchise.

Last Rites delivers on the franchise's usual brand of jumpscares & ghouls lurking in the shadows. It doesn't shy away from sentimentality in its goodbye to the Warrens, but it could have done more with its bloated runtime to bring their story full circle.
While Troll 2’s blemishes are part of its appeal, the film still manages to be fun, entertaining, and inventive for reasons outside of its “badness”. It is a very good bad movie.

Alien 3 immediately and completely squanders everything that made its predecessors great. This bold new vision swaps in a drab setting, unlikable characters, and an uninteresting plot that lacks suspense.
Together is a focused and powerful examination of personal identity and relationships that effortlessly balances its serious themes with its frequently playful tone.
House adds some interesting and original elements to the typical haunted house template, but it takes far too many detours that add little weight to the film’s themes or the impact of its conclusion.

media_title: I Know What You Did Last Summer
rt_quote: IKWYDLS is so busy cashing in on 90s nostalgia that it forgets to craft characters that matter and tests the boundaries of suspended disbelief. The kills somehow end up squandering the increased gore and suspense over the first film.
M3GAN 2.0’s genre pivot is a fun change of pace, but its overly complex plot and shoe-horned parental themes keep it from surpassing the original.

28 Years Later is both a return to the stylistic form of Boyle’s first entry in the franchise, as well as an upgrade. The film takes bold swings that are anchored by a heartfelt plot and excellent performances.

Ghostwatch’s commitment to realism hinders its ability to craft a compelling narrative, but the novelty of the approach, the early examples of found footage tropes, and a satisfyingly spooky ending make it a worthwhile addition to any Halloween watchlist.

This is a modernized rehash of the same shortcomings that have plagued the Friday the 13th franchise since its inception: weak characters and a lack of suspense. The rapid cuts to cameras in motion makes the film even worse than its 80s counterparts.
Bring Her Back begins by pulling some of the familiar levers of grief horror, but once things get violent, it doesn't take its foot off the petal and it becomes a fun yet dark and disturbing ride.

Scanners would benefit from more focus on its main character. The intricacies of its plot would be more potent if filtered through an expressive and complex character. But the ideas are captivating, the effects are impressive, and the score is incredible.
Final Destination Bloodlines takes itself seriously while simultaneously embracing its ridiculousness. The film does not forget to go big, especially in its jaw-dropping opening scene.

Suitable Flesh gets repetitive fast. It lacks an emotional core. By the third act, rather than wondering how things would get resolved, I simply found myself eager for an end to the villain's uninspired rants.

media_title: The Lair of the White Worm
rt_quote: The Lair of the White Worm lacks much substance. Its plot is scattered and at times rushed, but its casually humorous tone pairs well with the outrageous imagery sprinkled throughout.

The rich world, complex characters, and lush score of Sinners make for an all around wonderful experience. Music propels both the narrative and the film’s energy as gritty, soulful blues morphs into heavy metal in the film’s action-packed third act.

Drop begins as a stiff, paint-by-numbers, Blumhousian affair; but Fahy’s performance, a competent script, and tight direction ultimately buoy the strong premise as the tension flows organically in the final two thirds of the film’s efficient runtime.
Suspiria’s unifying theme is robbed of its potency by an inscrutable plot, opaque characters, and an excess of cinematic flourishes.

Final Destination is a vapidly entertaining film, with sleek production and effects making up for a lackluster plot and bland characters. The film’s bread and butter are its elaborate deaths, and on this front it mostly delivers.
